correctness.rationale: The two-sorted five-round EF proof correctly maintains equality, incidence and auxiliary triple-collinearity/concurrency for tuples of length at most three. At most three distinguished lines determine all needed fresh singleton/intersection/complement patterns uniformly for q>=4: the conservative complement q^2-2q-5 is positive there. On the final move with four prior variables, only atomic patterns are required, and the bound q^2-3q-3>0, plus q-2>0, supplies fresh realizations. Duality handles lines. The rank-four analogous bound works for q>=3. Three-line and four-line pencil-cover sentences Θ3 (rank four) and Θ4 (rank five) distinguish orders 2 and 3 from the stabilized larger orders. The concluding 42-element minimum is q=4 with 21 points and 21 lines. The separate C++ checker encodes normalized ternary projective coordinates and exact tuple-signature recursion, not a substitute for the infinite EF proof.
residual_risks: The preserved checker has an optimization for large tuple signatures; complete finite checks establish only stated small Desarguesian orders and cannot certify non-Desarguesian planes.

value.rationale: A complete rank-five classification for all finite projective planes, including non-Desarguesian, isolates the first new threshold after rank four and a sharp minimum 42-element model. Natural finite-model-theoretic invariant, not a relabeling or isolated tiny enumeration.
residual_risks: Only depth at most five; does not imply a general quantifier-rank hierarchy beyond that.

final_claim: Exactly three first-order quantifier-rank-five theories among all finite projective planes with named point/line sorts: q=2, q=3, and q>=4; rank four merges q>=3. Smallest representatives have 14,26,42 elements.
limitations: No assertions for unnamed sorts, collinearity as primitive, infinite planes, or rank >=6; priority risk from unindexed bounded-depth incidence logic results.
